content.one_sentence_role: Extends agreement from a convex interior to all source points by continuity.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $E,F$ be real normed spaces and let $f:S\to T$ be a bijective isometry between subsets. Assume $S$ is convex, its interior in $E$ is nonempty, and $$x\in\operatorname{int}_E(s)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(x)\in\operatorname{int}_F(t)\qquad(x\in S).$$ Then there is a unique surjective real affine isometry $A:E\to F$ such that $A(x)=f(x)$ for every $x\in S$.
content.assumptions: The stated interiors are ambient interiors, not relative interiors in affine spans. Convexity is assumed only for $S$. Both directions of the displayed interior-membership equivalence are hypotheses for the given $f$.
content.conclusion: The unique ambient affine extension agrees on all of $S$, including points outside its interior. No separate target convexity or completeness assumption is needed.
content.proof_summary: Restrict the isometry to the two ambient interiors, use the open connected theorem, and extend equality from the dense interior inside the source set.
proof_steps: For $x\in\operatorname{int}_E(s)$ the forward implication puts $f(x)$ in $\operatorname{int}_F(t)$. If $y\in\operatorname{int}_F(t)$, let $x=f^{-1}(y)\in S$; the reverse implication puts $x$ in $\operatorname{int}_E(s)$. Thus [The isometry restricted to ambient interiors](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Convex.lean#L24-L49) gives a bijective isometry $f:\operatorname{int}_E(s)\to\operatorname{int}_F(t)$, with the original forward and inverse values.

The source interior is convex and nonempty, hence connected, and both interiors are open. These verify every hypothesis of [Open connected extension theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/OpenConnected.lean#L120-L147) for the restricted isometry. It yields a unique ambient affine isometry $A$ with $A=f$ on $\operatorname{int}_E(s)$.

Convexity and nonempty interior give $s\subseteq\overline{\operatorname{int}_E(s)}$. Concretely, choose $c\in\operatorname{int}_E(s)$ and $\rho>0$ with $B(c,\rho)\subseteq S$. For $x\in S$ and $0<a\le1$, the point $x_a=(1-a)x+ac$ satisfies $B(x_a,a\rho)\subseteq S$ by convexity, and $x_a\to x$ as $a\downarrow0$. Thus the interior points are dense in the subspace $S$, the density step used in [Extension through a dense convex interior](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Convex.lean#L51-L95).

The two functions $A|_S$ and $f:S\to F$ are continuous. Their equality set is closed in $S$, because $F$ is a metric space, and contains the dense interior subset. Hence $A(x)=f(x)$ for all $x\in S$. Any other extension restricts to an extension on the source interior; uniqueness from Step 2 makes it equal to $A$.
